title: Registration done by the government from records it holds
parameters: Each state registers every eligible citizen it finds in its own motor vehicle and benefit records, and in the federal records it receives under CAP-19.02, and mails a notice with a way to decline (working choice: 21 days to decline before the registration takes effect). On the Australian model, where enrolment from records reaches 97.8% [EV-DEM-168] [EV-DEM-169]; Canada's register 96.4% [EV-DEM-170]. Today 28.0 million eligible citizens are not registered [EV-DEM-002]. *What it changes:* the National Voter Registration Act's opt-in agency registration becomes registration by default from records

A voter with none signs a statement of identity under penalty of perjury and casts a regular ballot, checked against records afterward. parameters: Every registrant receives a free voter card by mail from records: new registrants with the registration notice, and voters already on the rolls in a mailing phased over the first two federal election cycles after enactment, largest counties last (working choice, so offices are not swamped). A photo is optional: taken free at a state motor vehicle office, an SSA field office or the election office (working choice). The card is accepted as identification for every federal election in every state. No fee for any birth certificate or other record a voter needs to get a photo card. **The signed-statement route (DEM-1.06) stays:** the card is an option, never a condition of voting. Paid from DEM-11 (judgment: well under $0.1 billion a year). The national panel found strict ID had no effect on fraud [EV-DEM-154] (its abstract adds perceived fraud), so the card's case is ease and trust, not security alone

title: Citizenship checked against records, no documentary proof

No voter is required to bring a document to register or to vote. This is what keeps the rule inside *Inter Tribal Council*, which kept a state's power to deny registration on information in its possession and said a statute that kept a state from obtaining the information its qualifications need would raise serious constitutional doubts [EV-DEM-375]. The audits find noncitizen registration rare: 20 of 8.2 million in Georgia [EV-DEM-163], 27 of 2,069,640 records in Utah [EV-DEM-164]. *Diverges from* the House-passed SAVE America Act's documentary proof [EV-DEM-015]
